questions.question: What is the main advantage of using multiple attention heads in Multi-Head Attention (MHA)?
options: Each head can focus on different aspects such as grammar, context, or meaning
It eliminates the need for Keys and Values completely
It compresses memory more than MLA
It allows the model to skip attention

questions.question: Which statement best describes the main limitation of MHA mentioned in the chapter?
options: It requires storing many Keys and Values, increasing memory use
It only works with one attention head

questions.question: In MHA, the different attention heads primarily help the model to:
options: Learn different kinds of relationships in the input

questions.question: What problem does Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) mainly solve?
options: It reduces memory usage by sharing Keys and Values among multiple Query heads
It removes the need for queries altogether
It increases memory usage to improve accuracy
It stores more latent vectors than MLA

questions.question: Which component is shared among multiple Query heads in GQA?
Why is GQA considered more efficient than standard MHA?
options: It uses fewer Queries and no Keys
It reduces memory while keeping strong performance

questions.question: Which architecture is described as a newer improvement that reduces memory usage even further?
What is the key idea behind Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA)?
options: It stores large Key and Value data in multiple copies
It compresses Key and Value information into a smaller latent vector
It removes the need for reconstruction
It uses only one attention head

questions.question: In MLA, what happens when the model needs the original information again?
options: It discards the latent vector permanently
It reconstructs the original information from the compressed form
It asks the user to resend the prompt

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why MLA is efficient?
options: It stores more Keys and Values than MHA
It compresses information and reconstructs it when needed
It uses fewer attention heads than GQA only

questions.question: Which attention method is most directly associated with higher memory usage because of storing separate Keys and Values for many heads?
Which attention method allows multiple Query heads to use the same Keys and Values?
Which architecture is best described as compressing attention memory into a latent representation?
A transformer system needs to balance strong performance with lower memory usage. Which progression best reflects the improvements described in the chapter?
Which option best captures the trade-off in MHA?
options: Low memory usage but weak attention
High memory usage but rich attention across multiple aspects
No memory usage and no performance

questions.question: What makes GQA a practical compromise?
options: It keeps efficiency high while preserving strong model performance
It stores all Keys and Values separately
It only works for image tasks

questions.question: In which method are Keys and Values not stored in their full form but instead compressed first?
Which statement is most accurate about MLA compared with GQA?
options: MLA uses more memory than GQA
MLA reduces memory usage further by using latent vectors
GQA compresses information more than MLA

questions.question: The main reason Transformers use multiple heads in attention is to:
options: Make the model slower on purpose
Capture different aspects of the input simultaneously

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: MHA — shared Keys and Values among Query heads
GQA — compressed latent vectors with reconstruction
MLA — compressed Keys and Values stored as latent vectors
